result: PASS (author-run deterministic and real Chromium pairing evidence; mobile-data Tailscale UAT and independent acceptance are not tested)

checks.name: deterministic Core and Office gates
checks.detail: 268 Rust library tests passed, 13 Core binary tests passed, Clippy is clean, Office typecheck and Biome pass, 66 Office tests pass and the production build succeeds

checks.name: restricted Office pairing listener
checks.detail: the deterministic listener test proves access status requires an operator session, the current device is marked, a challenge can be claimed and approved with the matching code, the phone receives an independent session, the phone cookie is revoked, and the audit remains readable

checks.name: real desktop and phone Chromium journey
checks.detail: desktop enrollment, reload persistence, Settings to Access & Devices, QR challenge, phone claim, matching-code approval, independent phone session, challenge replay rejection, owner rejection, owner cancellation, single-device revocation, revoke-all and 1440/834/390 px layout passed

checks.name: PWA cache and credential boundary
checks.detail: the service worker registers with no cache entries; browser storage contains no operator token, bearer value, authorization value or session-shaped secret

checks.name: forged proxy identity
checks.detail: a forged x-tailscale-user header on an unauthenticated project request returned 401

checks.name: revoked-session shell recovery
checks.detail: a revoked phone cookie is cleared on the Office document request and the SPA renders its local recovery gate; protected API access remains denied

checks.name: audit and cancellation
checks.detail: Core returns a bounded session and pairing audit; cancellation is terminal, expired approvals cannot be consumed, and neither action creates a phone session

not_tested: mobile-data access from the owner's phone over Tailscale (USER_PENDING)
security_notes: The QR contains only a random challenge identifier. The phone receives a separate hashed poll capability, and Core creates a session only after the authenticated owner submits the matching verification code.
The phone session cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict. The CSRF token is a separate readable SameSite cookie used only in the x-factory-csrf header.
Revocation is immediate for protected API access. An invalid session cookie does not block the public Office shell; it is cleared so the app can show its recovery gate.
No pairing code, poll token, session cookie, CSRF value or operator credential is recorded in this evidence.
